header.name: Routing showcase
header.description: Five demonstrations of the routing extension: a pipe rack with concentric bends, a pair of counter-wound helical coils, a rectangular air distribution tree, a set of busbars on edge and a cable harness fanning out in space. All coordinates are global.

routing.name: Pipe rack
routing.description: Six titanium lines of a hydraulic system run side by side at a pitch of 45 mm: two turns in the horizontal plane and a climb over a beam in the vertical one. In the horizontal turns every line keeps its distance to its neighbours because its bend radius is the rack's radius minus or plus its own offset, so the six arcs share one centre. In the climb the offset lies across the plane of the bend, and all six take the same radius. Pressure and return lines alternate, 25 x 1.5 and 20 x 1.5 mm.

routing.name: Counterflow coil
routing.description: Two helical heat exchanger coils, one inside the other and wound in opposite senses, six turns each. Every turn is sixteen route positions on a circle, each rounded with a bend radius just below the radius of the coil, so the arcs nearly meet and the polyline reads as a helix. The outer coil is a 16 x 1.5 mm stainless tube, the inner one a 10 x 1 mm titanium tube, and both leave along their tangent at either end. 390 swept edges in all.

routing.name: Cabin air distribution tree
routing.description: A rectangular trunk under the crown, 200 x 100 mm, feeds three branches and narrows to 140 x 70 mm towards its far end. Each branch leaves sideways, dives towards the cabin at 60 deg and levels out again, reducing from 120 x 60 to 80 x 40 mm over the dive. Every bend lies in a horizontal or a vertical plane and none comes within 5 deg of the vertical, which is what a section with an orientation needs.

routing.name: Busbar set
routing.description: Three copper busbars of 40 x 6 mm standing on edge, a quarter turn of profileRotation, run a U round a distribution panel. They sit 25 mm apart, so their bend radii step by 25 mm about a common centre; standing on edge, each reaches only 3 mm towards that centre.

routing.name: Harness fan-out
routing.description: A cable bundle of 50 mm arrives at a breakout and fans into seven 12 mm conductors, spread evenly round the bundle's axis. Each bends away in its own plane, runs out, and bends back parallel to the bundle to reach its connector, so every one of the fourteen bends lies in a different plane.
